attachments.origin_landmark: iliacus: iliac fossa; psoas major: T12-L5 vertebral bodies/transverse processes (lumbar_vertebrae, not repeated as a 2nd origin_bone -- see compartment notes)

via_points.active_over_joint_range: all hip flexion angles -- the tendon wraps over the pelvic brim like a pulley

actions: psoas major also laterally flexes/stabilizes the lumbar spine

functional_compartments.name: Iliacus
functional_compartments.function_note: Fan-shaped, arises from the iliac fossa; joins psoas major's tendon just proximal to the lesser trochanter.
functional_compartments.source: Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset; Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

functional_compartments.name: Psoas major
functional_compartments.innervation_branch: lumbar plexus, direct branches from L1-L3 ventral rami (proximal to femoral n. formation)

neuromuscular_junction_zone.location_description: mid-belly endplate band -- for where this band lies along the muscle, see motor_endplate_zones

functional_compartments.function_note: Arises segmentally from lumbar vertebral bodies/discs and transverse processes; distinct innervation (direct lumbar plexus branches, not the femoral nerve trunk) from iliacus despite the shared distal tendon.
functional_compartments.source: Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset; Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

motor_endplate_zones.reference_line_to: the point where psoas passes under the inguinal ligament
motor_endplate_zones.method: stereoscopic microscopic dissection of intramuscular nerve branches
motor_endplate_zones.notes: An average of 3.7 nerve branches (range 2-7) enter psoas from the lumbar plexus. Expressed against the sacral promontory (P) instead, the limits run from 50% of the T12-to-P distance to 20% of the P-to-pubis distance. Endplate-targeted injection here produced measurable muscle atrophy where a more distal injection did not (Van Campenhout et al., Res Dev Disabil 34(3):1052-8, 2013, doi:10.1016/j.ridd.2012.11.016).
motor_endplate_zones.source: Van Campenhout A, Hubens G, Fagard K, Molenaers G. 'Localization of motor nerve branches of the human psoas muscle.' Muscle Nerve 42(2):202-7 (2010), doi:10.1002/mus.21660 -- stereoscopic microscopic dissection of 24 cadaver psoas muscles

motor_endplate_zones.notes: A single peak, on a reference line almost identical to the one Van Campenhout et al. used for the 30-70% range already recorded on this compartment. The two are compatible -- a peak sitting near the centre of a range -- and both are kept, because the range comes from direct cadaveric dissection and the peak from a clinical review, and neither supersedes the other.
motor_endplate_zones.source: Diaconu S et al. (Elias University Hospital), 'A Visual Guide to Ultrasound-Guided Botulinum Toxin Injection in Spasticity: Part III -- Proximal Lower Limb Muscles', Toxins 17(5):240 (2025), doi:10.3390/toxins17050240 -- review synthesis of the intramuscular neural arborization literature it cites

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Transverse (or longitudinal) on the posterior trunk, about 2 cm lateral to the L4 spinous process and 1 cm proximal to the iliac crest. Targets psoas major.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: From superficial to deep beside the L4 spinous process: paraspinal muscles, then quadratus lumborum lateral and superficial, then psoas major deeper, with the intraperitoneal space deep to psoas.
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: The approach exists to keep the needle out of the intraperitoneal space, which sits immediately beyond the muscle. In ambulatory patients psoas spasticity blocks hip extension in mid- and terminal stance; in non-ambulatory patients it drives poor seated posture and myotendinous retraction and complicates nursing care.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Diaconu S et al. (Elias University Hospital), 'A Visual Guide to Ultrasound-Guided Botulinum Toxin Injection in Spasticity: Part III -- Proximal Lower Limb Muscles', Toxins 17(5):240 (2025), doi:10.3390/toxins17050240 -- review synthesis of the intramuscular neural arborization literature it cites
